bull_bear.body: M&A focused on 'start small, scale fast' (4700BC, Plix); Synergy realization between True Elements and 4700BC; Prudent pricing hold to preserve premium vs. loose oil spread.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Copra price volatility timing; Bangladesh macroeconomic uncertainty; Delayed volume recovery in Parachute post-deflation; Integration execution of 4700BC into GT channels.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasizes 'purposeful acceleration' post-stability; Prudent on pricing (one-shot correction); Bullish on rural recovery and premiumization trends.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Parachute took only 60% price hike despite 100%+ copra spike, creating a buffer to absorb current 30% correction without immediate price cuts; 4700BC has high institutional/airline presence (Etihad, Air India) providing low-cost sampling vs. traditional marketing; Food growth pause is intentional to fix profitability before scaling, not demand failure.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - The only explicit capital-allocation language in this deck is the 'Grow Profitably' EDGE pillar, which states an intent to 'drive profitable growth through sharper portfolio choices, disciplined capital allocation, and focused investment behind growth engines' — a generic strategic statement with no dividend policy, buyback, payout ratio, or specific capex/M&A budget disclosed in the provided text; treated as a gap rather than filled.

business.body: India: VAHO double-digit growth (14% 2Y CAGR), Parachute volume stable post ml-reduction, Saffola Edible Oil soft due to pricing; Foods:Paused growth for profitability (Saffola Oats leading); International: Bangladesh robust, Vietnam/South Africa double-digit CC growth; Premium Personal Care: Exiting FY26 at INR 350cr+ ARR.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Deck claims India category leadership on a MAT Jun'26 basis: Parachute Rigids #1 in Coconut Oil at ~59% volume market share, Saffola Oats #1 at ~42%, Value Added Hair Oils #1 at ~29%, Post-wash Leave-on Serums #1 at ~44%, and Hair Gels/Waxes/Creams #1 at ~51%; footnote markers (^, *) accompany these figures but their legend text was not captured, so the exact basis (e.g. Nielsen) is not stated in the extracted text.
- Management attributes Parachute Rigids' quarter market-share gain (>400 bps, to a stated new high of 59%) to 'the brand's formidable equity, consumer trust and supply chain led competitive advantage' — this is the company's own framing, not an independent assessment.
- Strategy is organized around a stated 'EDGE' framework — Expand TAM and Portfolio, Distribution and Digitization, Grow Profitably, Empowered Organization — as the four pillars management says will drive the Vision 2030 topline ambition.
- MD & CEO Saugata Gupta frames the growth model as 'resilient core brands, accelerating premium and digital play, and a diversified international growth engine,' guided by a stated 'Fewer, Bigger, Bolder and Faster' philosophy toward Vision 2030.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [M&A/restructuring] Standalone financials were restated to reflect a restructuring of Zed Lifestyle Pvt Ltd and Apcos Naturals Pvt Ltd; recently acquired Foods brands 4700BC and Cosmix are described as delivering 'healthy sequential growth' during the quarter, i.e. still in early post-acquisition integration.
- [Accounting policy change] The deck discloses that certain customer-related Advertising & Sales Promotion expenses have been reclassified and are now netted off against Revenue from Operations (previously reported gross), applied retrospectively to prior comparative quarters; the company states this had no impact on EBITDA, Net Profit, Total Equity, Cash Flows or EPS — relevant for anyone comparing revenue/ASP figures across pre- and post-reclassification periods.
- [Awards] Marico's Legal Team was named 'Legal Team of the Year – FMCG' at the Legal Era Indian Legal Awards 2026; the Guwahati and Pondicherry plants received IMC RBNQA Milestone Merit Recognition 2025 certificates — reputational recognitions cited in the deck, not operational/financial claims.

deepdive.thesis: Marico delivered resilient Q3FY26 growth driven by double-digit VAHO expansion and international recovery, while strategically pausing low-margin food SKUs to pivot toward profitability ahead of a planned copra-led price cut. The acquisition of 4700BC fills a critical gourmet snacking gap, targeting a 3x ARR scale-up over three years alongside a guided 150-200 bps operating margin expansion in FY27 as input costs normalize.

open.item: Certain of getting back to 20-25% total Foods growth (organic plus inorganic) from next quarter, aided by 4700BC.
Premium Personal Care portfolio (serums, male grooming, skincare) expected to exit the year at ARR of Rs 350+ crore.

Copra down ~25-30% from peak; plan to pass benefit to consumers via a single one-shot price cut once copra trajectory is clear by March-April, possibly interim consumer offers, to support gradual volume recovery next year.
Confident of resuming accelerated growth in organic food business over the next two quarters, getting back to double-digit organic growth.

A Final Dividend of Rs 4.00 per equity share of Rs 1 each for FY2025-26, recommended by the Board on May 5, 2026, is to be paid on or before September 5, 2026 subject to Member approval at the 38th AGM.
open.promised: Rs 4.00 per equity share of Rs 1 each INR per share

open.item: Looking ahead to FY27, the Company will focus on strengthening its growth engines, deepening innovation capabilities and accelerating its sustainability agenda.
Digital-First portfolio to exit FY26 at ARR over Rs 1,000 crore; on track to reach 2.5x of FY24 ARR next year (FY27) with double-digit EBITDA margin by end of FY27.
Strive to improve operating margin by about 150-200 bps next year (FY27) as copra headwinds wane.
Expect progressive improvement in operating profit growth rates over the coming quarters as input cost eases; mid-teens operating profit growth as base case for next year (FY27).
Expect Bangladesh revenue share of international business to reduce to about 40% by FY27 (from over 50% in FY22).
Committed investment of INR 80-100 crore by FY27 for Project SETU, self-funded and cost-neutral (first-year outlay ~20-25 cr).
Expect Foods to reach ~50% of the Saffola franchise over the next three years, and 60%+ in five to seven years.
See tremendous potential for newly-acquired 4700BC (~Rs 140 cr ARR) to scale its ARR to 3x in the next three years, with a path to double-digit margin over time.
The Company is progressing against its ESG 2030 Roadmap, anchored in climate action, circularity, responsible sourcing, people well-being and robust governance.
The Company remains focused on its Vision 2030 aspirations, guided by a roadmap rooted in innovation, purposeful brand building and operational excellence.

Plix remains well positioned to drive accelerated growth over the medium term, backed by its digital-first community, focus on quality and efficacy and sustained innovation across effervescent supplements and personal care.

True Elements will continue to sharpen its focus on offline trade expansion to complement its strong digital-first presence, while Saffola Oats and Saffola Honey continue to invest behind distribution expansion and shelf visibility across General Trade, Modern Trade and E-Commerce.

Expansion of direct reach across urban and rural markets remains a strategic priority, supported by deeper rural penetration, improved in-store assortment and accelerated scale-up of new launches and the Foods portfolio across channels.

The next phase of Project SETU will focus on increased automation and AI-led resource optimisation to simplify processes, improve execution quality and reduce leakages, with advanced analytics supporting assortment, product mix and bill-value optimisation at scale.

The Marico Innovation Foundation will continue its Scale-Up programme supporting high-potential ventures across the circular economy, agri-tech and climate solutions, with the agri-pilot programme advancing to technology deployment after a baseline survey covering 1,000 farmers across Mirzapur and Varanasi.
